sentences.text: Janiosteus was a member of the class Placodermi, an extinct group of armored fish. It belongs to the family Panxiosteidae.
Ivanov described the genus Janiosteus in 1988, naming the type species Janiosteus timanicus. Fossils were found in Timan, Russia.
This animal lived during the Middle Devonian, specifically the Late Givetian stage. Its range extended from the Givetian to the Frasnian, between 387.95 and 372.15 million years ago.
A 2010 study suggested that the family Panxiosteidae was the sister taxon to Dunkleosteidae.
However, a 2016 study using a larger dataset placed Panxiosteidae outside Dunkleosteoidea, instead within Coccosteomorphi.
